The exact separate transmission by Amemar in Zevid’s name remains open. The readily identifiable direct source has Amemar speaking before Zevid of Nehardea, a different relationship and explicitly different heading.
The printed newer-edition reading remains a separate variant. The digital Bavli has Shmuel, while Heilprin writes Shimon. The article does not silently normalize either.
The specific paired versions await the exact witness. Meilah 19a directly supplies Kahana speaking to Zevid. The nearby related text did not yield this precise pair.
The original wrong locator and the compiler’s nonfinding remain visible. The eulogy itself is in Moed Katan 27b and specifically names Nehardea. The precise Yuchasin witness needs its own collation.

The classification as a pupil of Rav requires the direct Sheerit Yosef witness. The passages implicated in Heilprin’s argument attest Rav, Rabbah or Rava as distinct textual claims; the retrieved 84a gives Rabbah.
Heilprin’s correction between three name forms remains attributed. The checked 84a gives Rabbah and 85a gives Rava. The additional Rava occurrences are directly linked.
The exact locus for this form of address remains open. The Zeira–Zevid report is directly located but does not settle the chronological inference.
The exact expansion and range of print witnesses remain open. The bar and school forms occur in independently checked passages. Preserve Heilprin’s edition note and his conclusion separately.
The Rosh’s checked digital wording differs from this gloss. The version in Rosh gives bar Oshaya, as reported in the separate bar Oshaya entry. Printed editions require collation.
The printed edition sigla remain qualified. Direct Shevuot gives bar Oshaya and the separate Rabbi Oshaya chain.
